1#_: (Siman 102 seif 2) Or if the permitting matter is in his hand to do it. See in Kessef Mishneh (chapter 7 law 10 of Laws of Idolatry).
2#_: (Seif 4) Where the food spoils. Rashal in Yesh Seder (Chullin chapter 8 siman 87) disagrees — that this too is called something that has a permitted aspect.
3#_: (There in the hagahah) Every prohibition. It appears the opinion of Tosafot in Bava Kamma (daf 69) s.v. "everything gathered" is not so; and Magen Avraham already hinted to this (siman 318 s.k. 8); also so appears from Ran from what he wrote in Nedarim (daf 58a) on that which R' Shimon said "I too only said for removal" — see there: from the law of something that has a permitted aspect, even growths that were not recognizable by themselves are not nullified in the essence — see there.
4#_: (There) That was not recognizable. From this one can infer that likewise if wheat flour mixed with barley flour and afterward he vowed from wheat flour — it is nullified; although vows are something that has a permitted aspect, nevertheless at the beginning of the prohibition's formation it is mixed and the name of prohibition was never called upon it — so it appears simple, not as written in Mekor Chayim — see there at length.
